item.title: CKB Talk Daily Brief - 2026-10-17

item.title: QuotaCell: Let your team spend without handing over the treasury (1 posts)
item.description: Imagine you’re running a project with a small team. There are expenses to handle, suppliers to pay, and people who need to get things done. You can’t be available to approve every single payment. But you also don’t want to give everyone unrestricted access to the treasury. So how do you let people spend independently while keeping control of the funds? That’s the problem I’ve been working on with QuotaCell. Here’s how it works Say your project treasury holds 200 tokens. You want Alice and Ben to handle payments, but you’ve only approved 100 tokens for them to spend altogether. Alice has a personal limit of 70 tokens, and Ben has a limit of 50. Each can only pay their approved recipient....

item.title: [DIS] RIVET: Decentralized GitHub Backup, Timestamping and Restore on CKB (3 posts)
item.description: Nice work getting a working demo on testnet. Backup with a restore path is a real gap, and splitting restore into Exact and Attribution modes is the right call. Two technical points: 1. Anchoring for the deletion case. If GitHub deletes the repo, the anchor is the only independent reference left. What matters then is: does the restored copy match what was backed up? Anchoring a hash of the sorted refs and their tip commits answers that directly. After restore, anyone can recompute it from the bundle with plain git and compare it to the cell, with no GitHub and no Rivet server involved.
